sentences.text:
Order 
The petitioner claims to be CW5 in C.C No. 536/2025 on the file of the Court of Judicial First Class Magistrate, Alathur, which has arisen from Crime No. 499/2024 registered by the Alathur Police Station, Palakkad District, alleging the commission of the offences punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Court of Judicial First Class Magistrate, Alathur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The petitioner states that he is a jeweller by profession.
The petitioner has been served with Annexure A6 summons directing him to produce the gold ornaments that are involved in the above crime.
The petitioner has not received any gold ornaments from the accused persons.

Therefore,
Annexure A6 summons is illegal and improper.
Hence, the Crl.M.C.
3. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
The learned Public Prosecutor, on instructions, submits that, subsequent to the filing of the final report, further investigation was conducted.
The further investigation has revealed that the petitioner is involved in the crime.
Consequently, the petitioner has been implicated as an accused in the crime.
An additional report has been filed before the jurisdictional court.
In light of the above submission, Annexure A6 summons is unsustainable in law since the petitioner is made an accused in the crime.
Hence, Annexure A6 summons is quashed.
It would be up to the Investigating Officer to work out his remedies, in accordance with law, for the purpose of further investigation.
In the result, Crl.M.C is disposed of with the above observation.
